$comment: The driver's calendar (P12-31): PASS12-PLAN.md section 3.6 as blocks of UTC time on the run's three dates. It never says which date a case approves on: tools/budget-calendar.json does, and driver/schedule.py refuses any block whose date disagrees with it (one calendar, lane note 3). Every case of the case files is placed in exactly one block or listed under not_scheduled with its reason. driver/schedule.py checks each section 3.6 constraint against this file and the per-(principal, UTC date) budgets through tools/budget.py; A block's `refs` are the writes in it that no case owns (release/1.0 cut from main for case 33, rs-main from its tracked input), run before its cases; the checker walks them with the cases to hold release/1.0's and release/sandbox's preconditions. A block's `sequence`, when it has one, is the order its cases, snapshots, window ends and background changes run in (P12-32: a snapshot taken inside a window comes between the window's two ends); `setup` (the run's first steps, in the block marked setup), `windows`, `background`, `parts` and `scope` are described where they are declared. `driver.py --plan` prints it. Provisional: re-issued at the rehearsal gate and published at GO-4b as the intent file.

runs.$why: Each run's UTC dates. The rehearsal is R1 to R3 (Phase 5b, REG-114); the live dates are the provisional ones of section 3.6, fixed at the rehearsal gate (Phase 5c), then moved one day with GO-5 after a power cut on 11/11 (REG-781, REG-783).

swh.$why: The SWH queue's limits as measured at GO-2 (audit/p12-swhqueue-design.md, 4.2): 10 POSTs an hour, so a rolling cap of 9; the per-event lane always leaves 3 for the guaranteed lane and pauses in the hour before the freeze, when the guaranteed lane may take the whole cap. guaranteed_max_per_hour: the guaranteed lane needs at most 4 in one hour (the freeze's #3), and the checker refuses a fifth. The simulation over the calendar (driver/schedule.py, swh_simulation) takes the reserve, the pause, the window and the poll from witness/swh.py itself, a request's visit visit_seconds after it (GO-2's slowest of 2 to 9 s), a key moment's retry retry_after_seconds after its POST, and runs to the end of the /events tail, tail_after_freeze_hours after the freeze (PASS12-PLAN.md 3.6).

timing.$why: Measured or decided figures the checker holds the blocks to. save_1_worst_case: one save took 8h37m (DESIGN.md section 4, the Software Heritage row), so the flagship waits at least that long after setup (D12-10). freeze_after_period_end: FIX-E093. case_39_room: p11a.sh refused to start case 39 with an hour or less left in its UTC date. latency_floor is register/conditions.json's substance.latency_floor_sec, read at check time and compared here. quiet_window_after_seed: the quiet repository's window opens 1 s after its only commit (section 3.6; PASS0-DECISIONS.md section 5), derived by gen/register_derive.py from SAT_SEED_AT, and the checker holds this figure and that rule to it.

together.$why: Pairs section 3.6 moves as one group, so each runs in one block: multiple-independent-approvers with its D2.18 control, and case 21 with its control C3 (REG-114).

apart.$why: Minimal pairs with a case only the 1.0 history builds whose two cases run in different blocks, each with its reason. PASS12-PLAN.md 3.6 runs every minimal-pair control in the same block as its FIRE partner; P12-1D section 1 reads that rule as the newly designed controls' (the pairs of the retired history's own cases cross blocks, paired on the facts by tools/minimal_pairs.py). driver/schedule.py (pair_problems) refuses any other such pair split across blocks.

pairs.why: PASS12-PLAN.md 3.6 places C1 with p6b in the D1 16:00 to 18:00Z block, where rs-legacy, the ruleset it raises, is made, and case 48 straddles midnight by design (its day one before S9, its own write after it, before S10); the condition reads each ruleset's version history over the whole period, so no one block holds the pair

Falden, Inc.'s call (REG-254 item 2, 2026-10-04): the ride-along case's pair on approval.bypass_exempt_silent takes case 11 as its control (its below-minimum co-fire is a shadow since REG-745, 2026-11-06), which merges inside p3's zero-approval window in d1-p2-p3 (rs-main's count at 0, bypass_actors empty, S4 reading it), while the ride-along push lands inside p5's bypass window in d1-p5-p6 (the count at 2, OrganizationAdmin exempt, S6 reading it); the two windows put rs-main's pull_request rule in opposite states, so the zero-approval window and the bypass window cannot share a block

apart on purpose (REG-255 item 3): the pair is one ref at two instants, case 33's merge on release/1.0 before its classic protection (d1-batch-1, the window's first update) and case 41's push after it (d1-p5-p6), so a tool that stamps the ref's protection now on every change fails the control; one block cannot hold the merge, the protect between S2 and S6 and the push after S7

the co-fire's control (C14) is main's rewind, which brings no commit, made in the D2 rewind block under its own bypass window and the witness hold; case 41's push is read by D1's snapshots on each side, so the two cannot share a block

the not-evaluable slot's control (C14) is release/retired's deletion, which brings no commit; the witness hold places it on D2 once the SWH snapshot's target equals the live tip, and case 41's push is read by D1's snapshots on each side

holds.$why: PASS12-PLAN.md Phase 6, the witness hold: no step that removes or rewrites state runs until it is witnessed. Each case or event here must sit in a block marked hold.

scope.$why: The refs the declared scope holds (gen/register.py's ref_set: main, release/1.0, release/sandbox and the flagship release/retired on the subject repository, main on the quiet one). A snapshot reads the branch, its classic protection, its rules and its log for each of them that exists on the forge when it is taken (FORMAT.md 6.5; driver/ports.py, refs_in_scope); release/legacy is left out on purpose (protected-ref-not-in-declared-set).

windows.$why: A ruleset change a case's evidence needs open for that case only, then closed (P12-32; p2.sh, p3.sh, p4d.sh, p5.sh, p6c.sh). Each is opened and closed by a step of its own, named window:<name>:open and window:<name>:close in its block's sequence, with the cases it is for and any snapshot taken inside it between them. `from` is the tracked input the body is built from (inputs/rulesets/main.json), with the window's pull_request parameters, added rules and bypass actors applied; closing restores the input exactly. A role's bypass actor id is the one its token's /user showed, never typed. The owners are the cases the window is for; the driver journals each ruleset write with them.

stale-dismissal.why: dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push is switched on for this window only (gen/cases_part2.py; p2.sh)

zero-approval.why: required_approving_review_count lowered to 0 with bypass_actors empty, restored at once, both states snapshotted (gen/cases_part3.py; p3.sh)

merge-queue.why: a merge_queue rule added to the main ruleset and removed immediately after (gen/cases_part3.py; p4d.sh)

bypass.why: the count at 2, OrganizationAdmin exempt and the member an always-mode bypass actor, exactly one active ruleset on main, then bypass_actors empty and the count back to 1 (gen/cases_part3.py; p5.sh)

rs-temp.why: a dedicated disposable ruleset active on release/1.0, a pull request merged through it, S8, then deleted after its HOLD; never rs-main (gen/cases_part3.py; p6c.sh)

stale-dismissal-c2.why: dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push switched on for C2 alone and off again at once, so the forge dismisses its approval at the force push (gen/cases_part2.py, head-force-pushed-with-stale-dismissal-on); a window of its own beside p2's, since each window opens once

rewind-bypass.why: an OrganizationAdmin bypass in always mode, opened before the disposable commits land on main and closed after the rewind, so the rewind's rule suite records the bypass (approval.bypass_recorded) where exempt would record a pass with the rule skipped (gen/cases_part6.py; p8c-v2.sh, D8.1 and D8.4); closing restores the input exactly

parts.$why: A case whose mechanism runs in two blocks: the case is placed in the block of its own change, and the earlier part named here is placed in another block's sequence as part:<case>:<part>, before it, and before the snapshot `before` names, on that snapshot's date, and, when it names one, after the snapshot `after` names. The driver runs the part as a step of the case (driver/ports.py).

day-one.why: day one of case 48 (p7a.sh): rs-main's required approving review count raised from 1 to 2, then its enforcement moved active to disabled to active, each its own recorded write, before S9 snapshots the raised count; the case's own block, after midnight, lowers it to 1 before S10 (p7b.sh)

protect.why: case 41's classic protection on release/1.0 (REG-255 item 2), after S2, which with every read before it shows the ref unprotected around case 33's merge, and before S6, so S6 and S7 read the protection before the case's own push in d1-p5-p6 and S9 reads it after; a classic-only push writes no rule suite (measured once), so these reads decide the push

background.$why: Changes no case owns, each placed in its block's sequence as background:<name>. A background change is approved by the owner or by no one (REG-114). One that lands by pull request (`lands`) is counted in tools/budget-calendar.json's other_changes under `budget`, on the block's date (one calendar). One that edits a ruleset (`ruleset`) is a write no one approves (`approved_by` empty), so it moves no approval and no line, has no budget entry, and is built from a tracked input (`update.from`, with its pull_request parameters applied) on a ruleset an earlier write created. `before` names the cases that need it in place first.

bot-approve-workflow.budget: background: the dispatch-only workflow the machine cases run
bot-approve-workflow.why: landed the dispatch-only automation workflow bot-approve.yml, with its dispatch_id input and run name (attest design 2.4); support for the machine cases (p4a.sh)

minimum-cycle-0.why: D4.24's cycle, its first edit: rs-main's required approving review count lowered from 1 to 0, so 22a and 22b merge under 0 and the per-change minimum differs between changes (register minimum_rule); a ruleset edit no case owns and no one approves

minimum-cycle-1.why: D4.24's cycle, its second edit: the count raised from 0 back to 1; a ruleset edit no case owns and no one approves

minimum-cycle-2.why: D4.24's cycle, its third edit: the count raised from 1 to 2, so 23n merges under 2 with its two approvals standing; a ruleset edit no case owns and no one approves

minimum-cycle-restore.why: D4.24's cycle, its last edit: the count lowered from 2 to 1, rs-main its tracked input again before case 48's day one; a ruleset edit no case owns and no one approves

minimum_cycle.$why: D4.24 (audit/DEFECTS.md): the register publishes no scalar minimum, because the forge's required approving review count moves down as well as up while changes merge, and the minimum is read per change (gen/conditions.py: minimum_rule, minimum_per_change_field, minimum_observed_range). PASS12-PLAN.md 3.6 puts the cycle in the D1 independence block: rs-main's count walks this series through the block's background ruleset edits, each value other than the tracked input's held by at least one merge to main. driver/schedule.py (minimum_problems) walks rs-main's count through every block, window, background edit and case 48's two writes, and holds every case file's asserted count at merge and the register's observed range to it.

The satellite stays empty until case 8 seeds it on D2.
